A French-English education
in an outstanding environment
from an early age
L'Ecole des Petits
Pre-Primary Bilingual School
L’ECOLE DE BATTERSEA
We welcome children aged 3-6 into a happy bilingual family community
L’Ecole des Petits, French-English Bilingual school in Fulham offers a healthy and safe environment for our children to start their educational journey. We value their happiness and well-being above all.
We strongly believe that providing a bilingual education from the earliest age brings huge benefits to their development. Our curriculum takes the best from the English and French systems, and we mould them together to provide our children with a unique learning experience.
Our children are offered priority places at L’Ecole de Battersea when moving on to Primary (CP).

After School Care
We are pleased to announce that Fruity Club is now operating at our school with their after-school care service.
The provision will be as follows:
Operational days and hours for the afterschool care will be Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday from 3.30pm to 6.00pm and Wednesday from 12.00pm to 3.00pm. Please note that no bus service will be organised after the Fruity club.
School clubs already on offer will remain available from 3.30pm to 5pm on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays or from 12.00pm to 1.30/2.00pm on Wednesdays.
Children who attend an after-school club at L’Ecole des Petits can also attend Fruity Club afterwards at 5pm to 6.00pm (1:30pm – 4.00pm on Wednesdays).
Registration will be done on a first-come, first served basis and parents must commit to a regular weekly booking (e.g every Monday and Thursday or Monday, Tuesday and Thursday for example). Once registered, any communication/queries regarding Fruity Club should be directed at Fruity Club and not the school.
Fruity Club offers the following key services:
Quiet independent study & planned activities
Refreshments
Fresh air play
Fruity Club fees are £15 per session (£24 on Wednesdays)
Registration
You can register your child(ren) from today directly with Fruity Club. Please contact them at bookings@fruityclub.co.uk or 07786 966 187 (Nicky).

Our History
The evolution of L’Ecole des Petits
The foundation of L'Ecole des Petits
1977 L’Ecole des Petits was founded in 1977 by Mme Otten when she first came to London from Paris as a newly trained teacher to marry an Englishman. Finding that there were no established Ecole Maternelle in London at that time (only informal English nurseries and playgroups), she decided to set up her own school. She rented a church hall in South Kensington with a friend, decorated it, fitted it out and built furniture herself and started with five pupils aged three to five years old! The school followed the structured French curriculum for early years to which she added her own personal touches, including bilingualism. She understood the importance of this as she had been brought up in Italy and France, and was herself from an early age educated linguistically and culturally in both languages. At the time the project was unique, no other such bilingual establishment existed in London.
A dedicated building
1991 Parental demand for places became so strong that she decided to look for a permanent and more substantial base. She found a derelict former school building that had been empty since the 1950’s and set about renovating it.
The brief was to create a school with a “home from home” atmosphere so that children and parents alike would feel happy, safe and secure when they were at school. This ethos still underlies our schools today.
The building was of Victorian origin, and had previously been ‘The Princess Beatrice Social Centre’ for the Fulham Sands End area, inaugurated by the late Queen Mother, then Princess Beatrice Duchess of York, in 1931. The opening plaque still remains on the playground wall. Today the school caters for up to 130 children.
The foundation principle of international bilingualism and bicultural education from an early age became more and more of a feature of the school, providing specialised English and French classes for children aged between 3 and 5 years.
A recognised pre-primary school...
1995 L’Ecole des Petits became the first independent nursery school in the UK to be officially recognised as an Ecole Homologuée by the French Ministère de l’Education Nationale. Mme Otten was honoured as an “Officier des Palmes Academiques” by France for her contribution to International and French Education abroad.
...extending to primary education
2003 In 2003 the AEFE (Agence pour l’Enseignement Francais a l’Etranger) requested that L’Ecole des Petits extend its facilities to include primary education; this coincided with many parents asking the school to do the same. The Ottens followed up on this and came across the Salesians of Don Bosco former primary school building hidden away behind Battersea Square, just 10 minutes from L’Ecole des Petits in Fulham.
The start of L'Ecole de Battersea
L’Ecole de Battersea took form from this moment onwards. The school had originally been built in 1885, a typical church run Victorian school, with large rooms and high double height ceilings, and no central heating! Most classes in the Victorian time took place with tiered stadium type seating catering for a large number of pupils in one room, across age groups, what we today might call “open plan teaching.” The building had been empty for ten years since 1993 and had undergone little updating since its construction.
Mr & Mme Otten took the plunge, invested and working seven days a week non stop totally renovated the building over the six month period February – September 2005, new everything from sanitary ware, plumbing and heating system, to electrical, IT and technical infrastructure, sports and canteen facilities. They added two mezzanine floors with IT suite and library facilities, taking advantage of the high ceiling heights and redesigned the layout to create a modern and friendly primary school environment for the 21st century providing the same “happy, safe and secure environment” as at L’Ecole des Petits.
L’Ecole de Battersea opened in September 2005 with five classes and 85 pupils. Battersea now caters for up to 265 pupils.
The school rapidly gained widespread recognition and within two years established its position as an “Ecole Homologuée” with the French Ministry of Education and has since regularly achieved “Outstanding” in Ofsted inspections.
Today, the two schools continue to operate in conjunction with each other, providing a seamless bilingual education form age 3 (Petite Section/Nursery) to 11 years (CM2/Year 6).
“When you come to live in another country, you must adapt to the new customs, culture and language. This allows you to understand the people around you, all the while keeping your own identity.”
Mme Otten, founder

pageCache.pageTitle: Pre-Prep School (age 3 to 6) - L'Ecole des Petits - Fulham
pageCache.text:
Pre-prep school (age 3 to 6 )
Underlying our school ethos is the aim to encourage children to enjoy coming to school, to feel safe and to be happy there
This in turn makes them receptive to learning and allows us to open their minds, to encourage curiosity and to develop their characters and personal abilities. Building on this, the objective of our teaching is for them to master skills in both languages and develop an understanding of both cultures through being exposed to the specific qualities and characteristics of both the French and English educational systems.
Learning
We are not required to comply with the English Early Years Foundation Stage requirements. Since 2012, we have received an exemption from having to meet these in the areas of teaching and learning from the Department for Education. This exemption has been renewed in 2021.
Art, Dance & Sports
Art
Moyenne Section (Reception) and Grande Section (Year 1) music lessons, as well as Grande Section (Year 1) art sessions are led by a dedicated English teacher. Every year in May, an exhibition is held to display all pupils’ work.
Dance
All children have a weekly class of dance led by an experienced teacher who has graduated from the Royal Academy of Dance.
Pupils are taught physical expression through the use of their imagination and the teacher develops their sense of balance and coordination. During the year parents are invited to come and see a class.
Sports
From an early age we teach children to be aware of their bodies and to enjoy the pleasure of physical exercise both as individuals and as part of a team.
It is important for them to play at a young age so as to expend their energies and maintain a good health.
Every year in June, the school organises Sports Days by age groups.
Day trips
Being situated in the centre of London the schools are well placed to benefit from world-class theatres, museums, historical buildings, zoos, and many other attractions.
We are therefore very lucky that we can incorporate regular outings to a wide range of activities into our pupils’ learning process and awareness of the world around them. We also invite a variety of educators to visit the school to widen the children’s knowledge, such as artists, authors, illustrators and performers.
All knowledge expanding and stimulating for the children, and most importantly, fun for them!
“The well being of our pupils is very important, we work closely with parents and all the staff together to make that all our pupils are happy, they feel valued and safe.”
A teacher

Registration
We would be delighted to welcome your child when the time comes. Here is some information which will guide you through the process.
Starting school at 3 years old
As an Independent International School with a Nursery section, we welcome children from three years of age onwards.
In the case of our September intake, children who turn three between September and December of that year are also able to start (age 2 yrs 9 months +, known as rising three’s. They must be potty trained to start).
Children born in the same calendar year will therefore be in the same year group. For example children born in 2023 could start in September 2026.
Waiting list & priorities
As soon as we receive your application, your child will be added to the waiting list. On this list, we have the following priorities:
And then all new children are listed by registration dates, while also looking at the time between the birth and the registration.
There is a Registration fee to be paid when you make your application :
Siblings of former pupils
Children of former pupils
Being offered a place
Offers will be sent from October the year before starting. On acceptance of a place at the school for your child, a non-refundable admission fee is due.
New pupils joining in September must pay their first term fees in advance before 1st April in order to secure their place (see school terms and conditions).
Registering your child
The school office is open for registration from Monday to Friday, from 9.15am to 12.00pm and from 1.00pm to 4.30pm. The office is closed on Wednesday afternoons and during school holidays.
When you decide to proceed with the registration, please contact Ms Daniélou to request a registration package.
We encourage parents to visit the school before enrolling their children. School visits are conducted on Thursday mornings from October to May.
